title: How far from D must the corner B lie?
description: The corner B must lie on a line l, and the diagonal DB is seven centimetres. The video finds the second fact about B. Keeko's doubt is that B is seven centimetres from C, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: a diagonal joins two corners, so its length is the distance between exactly those two corners. Watch for students who measure the length of the diagonal from the wrong corner.

source: Line l is perpendicular to DC at C, and the point B must lie
video_script.why: A learner reads the diagonal's length as the distance between its two end corners, which gives a second fact about where B lies.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle ABCD with the line l at C and the diagonal DB of seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: the book's base DC with the line l at C and the corner B somewhere on l
video_script.wrong_answer: bee is seven centimetres from cee
video_script.wrong_move: takes the seven centimetres from the wrong corner, though it belongs to the diagonal that ends at dee
video_script.payoff_line: Bee is at a distance of seven centimetres from dee.

final_answer.spoken: bee is seven centimetres away from the point dee

maths_rules: the diagonal DB joins the corners D and B and is 7 cm long
so the distance between D and B is 7 cm
B also lies on the line l at C
B is the point of l that is 7 cm from D
video_script.design: The base DC and the line l stay on the board. A thread of seven centimetres is shown stretching from D, and the point where it reaches the line l is B.
